name: Deeplight
notes: A fish from the black bottom of the Thornspine tarns. It glows.
appearance: A black, eel-like fish whose belly glows a soft green, even after it's caught.

name: Skyfall Slag
notes: Black, glassy slag from the crater rim. Heavier than any rock that size should be.

name: Star-Iron Fragment
notes: A dark, pitted lump of iron from the meteorite. It pushes back faintly against your hand.

name: Starglass Shard
notes: Clear glass fused by the impact. Light inside it bends the wrong way.

name: Heart of the Fallen Star
notes: The dense core of the meteorite. It hums, it is never cold, and nothing quite wants to touch it.

name: Firestone Grit
notes: Yellow, foul-smelling grit from surface seams. Burns with a blue flame.

name: Cave Nitre
notes: White crust scraped from deep, dry rock. The heart of any blast powder.

name: Hollowreed Seed
notes: Hard little seeds from reeds along tarn edges. Steeped and sprouted, they ferment readily.

name: Bramblesweet
notes: Dark, sticky clusters from a thorny mountain bramble. Too sweet to eat many of; perfect for fermenting.
appearance: Dark, sticky clusters of tiny fruit, purple-black and glossy.

name: Cloudwasp Comb
notes: Pale wax comb from the nests of high-altitude wasps, heavy with golden syrup. Harvest it fast.

name: Grave Salt
notes: Grave Silt boiled down to grey crystals. Brainless will not cross a line of it willingly.

name: Bone Meal
notes: Ground bone and tooth. A binding and warding base.

name: Distilled Breath-Black
notes: Breath-black bile reduced to an ink-dark concentrate.

name: Iron Ingot
notes: A bar of smelted iron.

name: Rimecopper Ingot
notes: A cold, pale copper bar.

name: Thornspine Silver Ingot
notes: Bright silver from the Thornspine veins. Undead flesh burns where it touches.

name: Cut Emberquartz
notes: Emberquartz cut and polished to focus its warmth.

name: Whetstone Paste
notes: Slate grit bound in oil. Puts a hard edge on anything.

name: Wood Planks
notes: Cut and dried planks.

name: Ironbark Planks
notes: Ironbark cut into heavy planks.

name: Pitch Binder
notes: Pine pitch cooked into a waterproof, flammable binder.

name: Ashwood Haft
notes: An ashwood billet shaped into a flexible haft or limb.

name: Bitterleaf Extract
notes: A strong bitterleaf infusion. The base of most field remedies.

name: Moss Wadding
notes: Dried, pressed crag moss for packing wounds.

name: Hollowcap Toxin
notes: A clear, odourless toxin from boiled hollowcap.

name: Graveroot Tincture
notes: Graveroot steeped in spirit. Smells of turned earth.

name: Thistle Salve Base
notes: A soothing silver salve made from pale thistle sap.

name: Emberleaf Oil
notes: A red oil pressed from emberleaf. It warms the skin and burns bright.

name: Fish Oil
notes: Clear rendered oil. Burns long and clean.

name: Fish Glue
notes: Strong glue boiled from mudwhip skin.

name: Glassjaw Scales
notes: Cleaned, hardened glassjaw scales ready for stitching.

name: Cured Wolf Leather
notes: Wolf pelt cured into tough, warm leather.

name: Supple Stag Leather
notes: Soft, strong leather from tanned stag hide.

name: Cured Winter Fur
notes: Winter pelt cured with the fur on. Very warm.

name: Tanned Bear Hide
notes: A whole bear hide tanned thick. Heavy, but turns blades.

name: Rendered Tallow
notes: Bear fat rendered clean. Waterproofs, fuels and soothes.

name: Star-Iron Ingot
notes: Meteoric iron worked into a bar. Blades made from it hit harder than their weight.

name: Meteoric Flux
notes: Ground skyfall slag. A pinch lets star-iron bond with ordinary metal.

name: Charcoal
notes: Pine burned slow and airless. Fuel, filter and a third of every blast powder.

name: Blast Powder
notes: Grey-black powder that goes up with a flash and a bang. Keep it dry and far from flame.

name: Fuse Cord
notes: Pitch-soaked cord packed with powder. Burns about a foot every few seconds.

name: Hollowreed Mash
notes: Sprouted, crushed hollowreed seed left to sour. The base of most brews.

name: Distilled Alcohol
notes: Clear, harsh spirit run off a still. Drinkable in a pinch; mostly used by alchemists.

name: Stripped Rib
notes: A rib picked clean long ago. The Ageless it held up stopped needing flesh decades back.

name: Bone Dust
notes: Fine grey powder that sifts out of old skeletal joints.

name: Rusted Mail Links
notes: Corroded rings from mail worn by something that no longer bleeds.

name: Grave-Cut Arrowhead
notes: A bone arrowhead carved by fingers with no skin on them.

name: Hollow Vertebra
notes: A spinal bone worn smooth from centuries of turning.

name: Skull Splinter
notes: A piece of the skull that held the mind. Once it broke, the rest of the skeleton fell.

name: Pitted War-Steel
notes: Old blade steel, pitted but sound. The skeleton kept it sharp.

name: Socket Ember
notes: The cold light from an empty eye socket, caught in a chip of bone before it faded.

name: Mouldered Spell Page
notes: A page of spell notes in a hand that has not changed in centuries.

name: Grave-Black Plate Shard
notes: Armour plate blackened by long years in the dead lands.

name: Unyielding Femur
notes: A thigh bone gone as hard as iron. It never broke, however often it was struck.

name: Oath-Etched Heraldry
notes: A rusted crest from a knight's shield. The order it names no longer exists.

name: Marrow Ink
notes: Dark ink pressed from necrotic marrow. Skeleton mages write with nothing else.

name: Bone Focus Rod
notes: A forearm bone carved into a casting rod. It points toward the nearest corpse.

name: Unerring Finger Bones
notes: The draw-hand of a skeleton archer, still curled around a string that isn't there.

name: Knight's Anchor Skull
notes: A skeleton knight's skull, cracked open. A mind lived in it, and a sense of duty older than the Compact.

name: Whispering Skull
notes: A skeleton mage's broken skull. It still mutters half-finished spells.

name: Death-Tempered Steel
notes: Steel quenched again and again in a death knight's cold until it took the cold for itself.

name: Fallen Oath-Blade Shard
notes: A broken piece of a death knight's sword. It remembers every blow it landed.

name: Heart of a Broken Oath
notes: Cold black crystal grown inside a death knight's ribcage, where a heart used to be.

name: Grave-Crown Circlet
notes: A lich's circlet of bone and black iron. Cold enough to burn.

name: Lich's Held Breath
notes: A sealed vial of breath a lich drew from the dead lands and never let go.

name: Lich-Skull Shard
notes: A shard of a lich's skull. Breaking the skull is the only way to end one, and the shard remembers being whole.

name: Ram's Wool
notes: Coarse, oily wool shorn from a mountain ram. Spins into warm, water-shedding yarn.

name: Curled Horn Chip
notes: A chip of ridged ram horn. Grips well and doesn't slip when wet.

name: Thick Fleece
notes: A whole fleece from a ram that wintered on the high ledges.

name: Spiral Ram Horn
notes: A full curled horn, hard and springy.

name: Old Ram's Horns
notes: The battered horns of a ram that won every fight on its ledge.

name: Silent Paw Pad
notes: A snow cat's paw pad, soft as felt. It makes no sound on stone.

name: Snow Cat Fang
notes: A long, thin fang made for one quick bite to the neck.

name: Ghostfur Pelt
notes: White pelt that is almost impossible to see against snow.

name: Hunter's Whisker
notes: A snow cat whisker. It trembles before anything moves nearby.

name: Snow Cat Eye
notes: A pale eye that saw through blizzards. It still catches light in the dark.

name: Bristle Hide
notes: Thick hide covered in stiff black bristles.

name: Boar Tusk
notes: A short, sharp tusk. Makes a good hook or awl.

name: Thick Boar Hide
notes: Heavy, wind-proof hide from an old tuskback.

name: Great Tusk
notes: A tusk as long as a forearm.

name: Tuskback Heart
notes: The heart of a boar that charged until the very end. Cooks rich and dark.

name: Black Crow Feather
notes: A glossy black feather. Stiff enough to fletch.

name: Grave-Fed Crow Eye
notes: The eye of a crow that fed on Brainless. It turns toward the dead on its own.

name: Crow Gizzard Stone
notes: A polished stone from a crow's gizzard. Perfectly round.

name: Murder-Black Plume
notes: Tail plume from the crow that led the flock. The others still follow it.

name: Bat Wing Membrane
notes: Thin, tough wing skin from a cave bat.

name: Bat Guano
notes: Dried cave droppings. Leached and boiled, they give up nitre.

name: Echo Bone
notes: A tiny skull bone that rings when sound bounces off it.

name: Night-Ear
notes: The great folded ear of an elder bat. Hears a heartbeat through stone.

name: Serpent Scale
notes: A dinner-plate scale from a tarn serpent. Hard and slick.

name: Tarn Serpent Fang
notes: A curved fang longer than a finger.

name: Serpent Hide
notes: Smooth, water-proof hide from a tarn serpent's belly.

name: Venom Sac of the Deep
notes: A tarn serpent's venom sac. The venom stays cold and potent for months.

name: Tarn Serpent Heart
notes: A huge, slow heart that beat once a minute in the cold deep.

name: Breath-Matted Pelt
notes: A Brainless beast's pelt, matted with breath-black. The dead don't seem to notice whoever wears it.

name: Hollow Howl
notes: The throat of a Brainless wolf. Air pushed through it still howls, and the dead come.

name: Deadweight Paw
notes: A Brainless bear's paw, heavy as an anvil and still clenched.

name: Breath-Burst Heart
notes: A swollen heart packed with old breath. It bursts at the lightest cut.

name: Fused Bone Knot
notes: Bones from a dozen bodies grown together into one hard knot.

name: Bloom Ichor
notes: Thin grey fluid from an amalgam. Corpses it touches will not rise again.

name: Bloom Seed
notes: The catalyst at an amalgam's centre. Handle it as if it were about to go off, because it might.

name: Ritual Ash
notes: Ash from a Waking rite, carried in a pouch. It smells of cold stone.

name: Breath-Prayer Strip
notes: A cloth strip lettered with prayers to Varreth, worn wrapped around the wrist.

name: Ceremonial Knife
notes: A thin ritual blade. Cheap steel, but kept very sharp.

name: Exhale-Stained Gloves
notes: Gloves worn while handling the dead. Stained grey to the wrist.

name: Coded Waking Letter
notes: A letter in a simple cipher. Someone was meant to burn it.

name: Waking Sigil Ring
notes: A ring stamped with the Waking's mark. The Directed Brainless hesitate when they see it.

name: Frayed Compact Tabard
notes: An Ironwall Compact tabard with the insignia cut off.

name: Spent Compact Bolts
notes: Compact-issue crossbow bolts, bent or missing their fletching. The heads are still good.

name: Compact Crossbow Parts
notes: The prod, trigger and windlass of a Compact heavy crossbow.

name: Ironwall Patrol Map
notes: A worn map of patrol routes and safe passes behind the Wall.

name: Compact Signal Horn
notes: A brass signal horn. Every soldier on the Wall knows its calls.

name: Woven Wool
notes: Ram's wool spun and woven into a thick, oily cloth.

name: Raw Game Meat
notes: Mixed trimmings from whatever the hunters brought in. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A mixed heap of dark red trimmings in odd shapes and sizes, wrapped in cloth.

name: Wolf Neck
notes: Stringy neck meat. Best stewed for hours. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: Thin ropes of dark, stringy meat around a column of knobbled bone.

name: Wolf Shank
notes: A sinewy foreleg shank. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A narrow foreleg, the meat wrapped tight in silvery sinew.

name: Wolf Shoulder
notes: The meatiest part of a wolf, and still lean. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A flat, deep-red slab, lean and laced with grey connective tissue.

name: Wolf Backstrap
notes: The long muscle along a wolf's spine. Surprisingly tender. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A long, narrow strip of almost purple meat with no fat on it at all.

name: Stag Neck
notes: A thick neck roast. Wants slow cooking. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A thick, round roast of deep maroon meat, marbled with white sinew.

name: Stag Shank
notes: Lower leg, all connective tissue. Rich when braised. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A short leg section, the dark meat glossy with silvery tendon.

name: Stag Brisket
notes: Thin breast meat between the forelegs. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A thin, layered flap of red meat and pale fat from the chest.

name: Stag Shoulder
notes: A whole shoulder roast. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A broad, uneven roast, dark red, with a flat blade of bone inside.

name: Stag Rib Rack
notes: A rack of ribs, lean and dark. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A curved row of slender ribs with a strip of dark meat along the top.

name: Stag Hindquarter
notes: The big muscles of the rear leg. Roasts or slices into steaks. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A heavy, tapering leg of tight-grained, dark red muscle.

name: Stag Backstrap
notes: The loin along the spine. The cut every hunter wants. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A long, smooth cylinder of deep crimson meat, perfectly lean.

name: Stag Tenderloin
notes: Two small strips from inside the ribcage. The most tender meat on a stag. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: Two small, soft strips of dark red meat, smooth as velvet.

name: Hawk Thigh
notes: Dark thigh meat. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A small curl of dark, almost brown meat on a slender bone.

name: Hawk Drumstick
notes: A lean drumstick. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A thin drumstick, tight-skinned and lean, the skin speckled grey.

name: Hawk Wing
notes: More bone than meat. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A folded wing of skin and fine bone, more tendon than meat.

name: Hawk Breast
notes: The flight muscle. Dense, dark and plentiful for a bird. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A dense, dark breast the size of a palm, deep red rather than pale.

name: Bear Neck
notes: A heavy, fatty neck roast. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A huge, fatty roast, the dark meat streaked with yellowish fat.

name: Bear Shank
notes: A massive shank, thick with sinew. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A leg section as thick as a forearm, wrapped in heavy sinew.

name: Bear Shoulder
notes: A shoulder roast as big as a man's chest. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A massive dark roast the size of a child's torso, heavy with seams of fat.

name: Bear Ribs
notes: A slab of rich, fatty ribs. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A broad slab of thick ribs under dark meat and a rind of creamy fat.

name: Bear Haunch
notes: A whole hindquarter, heavy and dark-meated. Wants a long, slow braise. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A whole hindquarter, dark as wine, under a thick cap of yellow fat.

name: Bear Backstrap
notes: The loin along a bear's spine. Dark, rich and tender. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A long, heavy loin of near-black meat with a thin seam of fat.

name: Bear Tenderloin
notes: The inner loin. Rare to get out whole. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A long, soft, dark loin, surprisingly fine-grained for something so big.

name: Ram Neck
notes: Bony neck slices for the pot. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: Bony rounds of pink-red meat around thick vertebrae.

name: Ram Shank
notes: A meaty foreshank. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A stubby, meaty shank with a creamy cap of fat.

name: Ram Breast
notes: Fatty, thin breast meat. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A thin, flat sheet of meat layered with soft white fat.

name: Ram Shoulder
notes: A marbled shoulder roast. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A rounded, marbled roast, pink-red with ribbons of fat.

name: Ram Loin Chops
notes: Thick chops cut from the loin. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: Thick chops shaped around a bone, each with a rim of firm white fat.

name: Ram Leg
notes: A whole hind leg for roasting. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A whole hind leg, rounded and pale-skinned, the meat a rosy red.

name: Ram Rack
notes: A rack of rib chops, trimmed clean. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A neat row of rib chops, the bones scraped clean and curving like a crown.

name: Ram Saddle
notes: Both loins still joined along the backbone. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: Both loins still joined along the backbone: a long double roast under a cap of fat.

name: Boar Jowl
notes: Fatty cheek meat. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A thick, square cheek, mostly pale fat with streaks of pink meat.

name: Boar Hock
notes: The lower leg joint. Boils down rich. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A knobbly joint in thick, bristled skin, the meat packed around the bone.

name: Boar Trotters
notes: The feet. Mostly for broth. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: Split hooves in pale, bristly skin. Mostly bone and gristle.

name: Boar Belly
notes: A slab of fatty belly. Crisps beautifully over coals. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A thick slab of alternating pink meat and white fat under bristly skin.

name: Boar Shoulder
notes: A heavily marbled shoulder roast. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A big, heavily marbled roast, deep pink and streaked with fat.

name: Boar Spare Ribs
notes: A rack of meaty spare ribs. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A long rack of curved ribs under a layer of dark pink meat.

name: Boar Ham
notes: The whole hind leg. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A whole hind leg, round and heavy, the meat a deep rosy pink.

name: Boar Loin
notes: The long loin along the back. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A long, even loin of dark pink meat under a thin cap of fat.

name: Boar Tenderloin
notes: The small inner loin. Hardly any fat at all. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A slim, tapering strip of deep pink meat with hardly any fat.

name: Serpent Rib Meat
notes: Strips of pale meat picked from between a tarn serpent's ribs. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: Long, thin strips of pale, almost see-through meat, cold to the touch.

name: Serpent Fillet
notes: A long, firm fillet. Cold to the touch even after it's cut. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A long, firm fillet of white meat with a faint blue sheen.

name: Serpent Backstrap
notes: The muscle running the serpent's whole length. Prized and rarely taken whole. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A rope of pale, dense muscle as long as a man, glistening and cold.

name: Shark Fillet
notes: Coarse, salty shark fillet. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A coarse, grey-white fillet that smells strongly of the sea.

name: Shark Steak
notes: A thick steak cut across the body. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A thick round steak of pinkish-white meat around a ring of cartilage.

name: Shark Belly
notes: Rich, fatty belly meat. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A pale, fatty strip, soft and almost creamy.

name: Shark Loin
notes: The thick loin along a big shark's back. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A thick block of firm, rose-tinted meat, the best part of a big shark.

name: Crab Leg Meat
notes: Sweet white meat from the legs. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: Long, sweet strands of white meat with red edges, pulled from the shell.

name: Crab Body Meat
notes: Flaky meat from the body. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: Loose flakes of soft white meat picked from the body shell.

name: Crab Claw Meat
notes: Dense meat from the great claw. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A dense, fist-sized lump of white meat streaked with red.

name: Octopus Tentacle
notes: A thick tentacle. Tough unless cooked right. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: A thick, mottled purple-grey tentacle lined with pale suckers.

name: Octopus Mantle
notes: The head, sliced into tender rings. Spoils in a few days unless cooked or cured.
appearance: The smooth, rounded body, sliced into pale rings.

name: Scree Tuber
notes: A starchy mountain tuber that grows among loose stones. Bakes soft and earthy.
appearance: A knobbly grey tuber the size of a fist, so like the scree it grows in that foragers find it by kicking stones.

name: Frostcurl
notes: Young fern shoots, eaten before they unroll. Crisp and grassy; eat them cooked.
appearance: Tight green spirals of young fern, rimed with frost even in the hand.

name: Snowstalk
notes: A sharp, eye-watering stalk that flavours a whole pot.
appearance: A hollow white stalk as long as an arm, with a papery blue tip.

name: Ashbulb
notes: A bitter, smoky bulb that grows only along the ashline.
appearance: A black-skinned bulb; cut open, its flesh sits in grey rings like old ash.

name: Cragberry
notes: Hard, sour little berries from thorny crag shrubs. Best dried.
appearance: Hard little red berries clustered on thorny grey shrubs.

name: Rimepod
notes: A pod-fruit that only sweetens after a hard frost. Cold, sweet and faintly fizzy.
appearance: A pale blue pod the length of a thumb, hard until a frost, then soft and glassy.

name: Embergourd
notes: A gourd that grows in the warm hollows and never cools, even off the vine.
appearance: A squat orange gourd, warm to the touch; its flesh glows a faint red when cut.

name: Smokewort
notes: A downy herb that tastes like woodsmoke. Rubbed into meat before roasting.
appearance: Grey, downy leaves that smell exactly like a dying campfire.

name: Sharpneedle
notes: A resinous, needle-leafed herb. Piney and sharp; a little goes a long way.
appearance: Stiff, needle-thin green leaves on a woody stem, sticky with resin.

name: Saltmoss
notes: A crusty moss from wet rock that tastes of salt. Foragers season with it.
appearance: A crusty, white-green moss that leaves salt on your fingers.

name: Tull
notes: The staple root of Valdren farms. Dense, sweet when roasted, and keeps all winter.
appearance: A heavy, round purple root with bright orange flesh.

name: Kesh
notes: A leafy head grown in every Valdren kitchen garden. Mild cooked, peppery raw.
appearance: A tight head of crinkled dark-green leaves, as big as two fists.

name: Varn
notes: Pod-beans dried by the sackful. The Compact feeds the Wall on them.
appearance: Long yellow pods split open on fat, white beans.

name: Orrel
notes: A small, crisp orchard fruit from the Valdren lowlands. Tart, and good stewed.
appearance: A small, hard yellow fruit with a red blush on the side that faced the sun.

name: Dunsk
notes: A winter-keeping fruit stored in cellars. It sweetens as it shrivels.
appearance: A dark, wrinkled, near-black fruit that looks spoiled and tastes sweeter for it.

name: Tidecress
notes: Salty greens picked from tide pools at low water.
appearance: Glossy, dark-green sprigs, beaded with salt from the tide pools.

name: Sailor's Knot
notes: A twisted island root that keeps for months in a ship's hold.
appearance: A twisted, knotted brown root, as if someone had tied it in a bowline.

name: Sourbell
notes: A jaw-achingly sour fruit. Sailors eat it to keep their teeth, and the peel flavours cheap rum.
appearance: A bright yellow fruit shaped like a bell, its thick peel shiny with oil.

name: Bloodpod
notes: A red island fruit full of crimson juice. Sailors swear it's why the sea is red.
appearance: A red, leathery pod that bursts with crimson juice when you bite it.

name: Galleyweed
notes: Dried seaweed flakes kept in every ship's galley. Salty and savoury.
appearance: Brittle grey-green flakes of dried seaweed, kept in a stoppered jar.

name: Alchemist's Blue
notes: A rare blue fruit from a handful of remote islands. It tingles on the tongue.
appearance: A smooth, vivid blue fruit that crackles faintly when you squeeze it.

name: Crag Nest Egg
notes: A small, speckled egg from a cliff nest. Strong-tasting.
appearance: A small egg, brown and heavily speckled, about the size of a walnut.

name: Reedfowl Egg
notes: A pale green egg from a nest in the tarn reeds. Rich yolk.
appearance: A smooth, pale green egg with a thick shell.

name: Coop Egg
notes: A farmyard egg from the Valdren lowlands. Sold by the dozen.
appearance: A plain brown egg, sold twelve to a straw-lined basket.

name: Skerry Egg
notes: A big seabird egg collected from rocky islets. Fishy if fried.
appearance: A big, pointed egg, blue-white and blotched with black.

name: Hawk Egg
notes: A crag hawk's egg, taken from the nest of a hawk that defended it.
appearance: A grey egg streaked with rust-red, warm if it's fresh from the nest.

name: Serpent Egg
notes: A tarn serpent's egg, leathery and cold. One makes a meal for four.
appearance: A leathery, off-white egg as big as a melon, cold to the touch.

name: Crab Roe
notes: Bright orange eggs from a giant crab. A delicacy in every port.
appearance: A heap of tiny, bright orange beads that pop between your teeth.

name: Coarse Flour
notes: Ground seed or grain. The start of any bread.
appearance: A sack of gritty, pale brown flour flecked with husk.

name: Hearthbread
notes: A flat round of bread baked on a hot stone. Folds without breaking.
appearance: A flat, round loaf a hand thick, freckled black where it touched the stone.

name: Valdren Curd
notes: A crumbly white farm curd, sold wrapped in leaves.
appearance: A crumbly white wheel wrapped in broad green leaves.
